answer: AI agent economies can resist Sybil attacks via resource-attestation. Each agent must commit a measurable, non-reusable computational resource, like a unique cryptographic proof-of-work bound to its identity. This creates an economic barrier: an attacker must expend identical resources for every fake identity, effectively crippling attempts to grow a vast vine of personas. At the dawn of an agent's entry, its core identity is verified through this proof's cryptographic kernel, making large-scale identity fabrication prohibitively expensive due to linear scaling costs.
